title: Pictograms / Tints and shades — Dark background

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Dark background

slide_intent: Add tonal depth without sacrificing the pictogram’s outline, because the underlying metaphor must remain readable when fills become expressive.
strategic_value: Controlled blue shading can give IBM pictograms additional character while preserving a coherent line vocabulary.
demonstration: Eight blue pictograms form two rows on a dark-blue field, combining brighter outlines with darker tinted or shaded regions.
practical_value: Keep the identifying strokes distinct from the fill when adding shade on a dark background.

content_islands.name: Background selector
content_islands.spec: Show Dark background selected in the tab row.

content_islands.name: Upper specimens
content_islands.spec: Arrange four examples including a mortar-and-pestle, network form, switches and heart with arrows.

content_islands.name: Lower specimens
content_islands.spec: Continue with a branching diagram, geometric groups, calendar and pointing hand.

ingredient.name: Shaded pictogram fill
ingredient.role: Add depth while preserving the identifying outline.
ingredient.application: Use approved families and keep strokes accessible; on Black or value 100 backgrounds, choose fill shades one or two steps down as stated in the source.
ingredient.scope: The numeric fill rule is explicitly for Black/value 100 in the accompanying guidance; this specimen demonstrates the general dark-background treatment. It does not establish a new universal fill ratio.

reference_purposes.Expression: The specimens demonstrate blue tonal variation within simple pictogram linework.
reference_purposes.Application: The examples show how dark fills and brighter strokes can coexist on a dark field.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying tint/shade guidance permits one- to three-color families, recommends one family, and requires accessible strokes and the stated five-step rule.
